scope: Inventory of the injected-failure suites that already exist in the worker and Rust code. usage:fault-matrix runs every listed suite and fails when one is missing, renamed, skipped or not passing. It adds no fault tests of its own.

failureClasses.crash-before-effect: The process or request dies before its durable effect; recovery must show no partial write and an exact retry succeeds.
failureClasses.crash-after-effect: The process dies after the effect but before acknowledgement; recovery must resume without a second charge or duplicate publication.
failureClasses.disk-full: Local persistence refuses a write for lack of space and the ledger stays consistent.
failureClasses.capacity-exhaustion: Durable Object or storage capacity refuses new work before any index write; the last published state is retained. The nearest existing analog to disk-full.
failureClasses.lost-reply: A committed write, RPC or grant reply is lost; an exact retry reconciles without duplicating the effect.
failureClasses.restore-race: A stale, reordered or late actor races a restore, reopen, fence or cancellation and must not mutate canonical state.

gaps.reason: No existing local-persistence test injects ENOSPC or SQLite full-disk errors. capacity-exhaustion suites are the nearest analog and are listed as such, not as disk-full evidence.

refuses a stale epoch after publish
lost grant replies reconcile the exact attempt, including after close
terminal cancellation fences both reordered future grants and granted-but-lost replies
capacity refuses new attempts while existing unknown grants still reconcile and cancel
lost committed PUT reply preserves the object and reconciles on an exact later retry
a lost readback is not a successful persistence receipt
closed fences prevent object access or withhold success after an uncertain write
real HTTP/RPC commit survives a lost RPC reply and restart without duplicate publication
